questions.q: When did Daniel have his second vision?
questions.a: Daniel had his second vision in the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar.

questions.q: Where was Daniel in his vision?
questions.a: Daniel was in the fortified city of Susa in the province of Elam beside the Ulai Canal.

questions.q: What were the two animals Daniel saw in this vision?
questions.a: Daniel saw a ram and a male goat in this vision.

questions.q: What were the ram’s two horns like?
questions.a: One of the ram’s horns was longer than the other, but the horn that grew later eventually became the longer one.

questions.q: How powerful was the ram?
questions.a: No animal could stand before the ram. None could be rescued from the ram’s hand. It did whatever it wanted, and it became great.

questions.q: What kind of horns did the goat have?
questions.a: The goat had only one large horn between its eyes.

questions.q: How did the goat approach the ram?
questions.a: The goat ran at the ram in great anger.

questions.q: What did the goat do to the ram?
questions.a: The goat struck the ram, broke off its two horns, knocked it down to the ground, and trampled on it.

questions.q: When the large horn of the goat was broken off, what grew in its place?
questions.a: Four other large horns, pointing north, south, east, and west, grew up in place of the one that was broken off.

questions.q: What happened to one of the goat’s four horns?
questions.a: Out of one of the horns grew another horn, small at first, but it became very large toward the south, the east, and the beautiful land of Israel.

questions.q: What did this horn do when it became large?
questions.a: It grew strong enough to attack heaven’s army, throwing some of the army and some of the stars down to the earth and trampling on them.

questions.q: What did this horn do to the commander of heaven’s army and his sanctuary?
questions.a: It stopped the daily sacrifices to Yahweh, the commander of heaven’s army, and it ruined his sanctuary.

questions.q: Why will the army be given over to the goat’s horn and the burnt offering stopped?
questions.a: This will happen because of rebellion.

questions.q: What did Daniel hear one holy one ask another?
questions.a: He heard one ask how long the vision about the sacrifices being stopped, the sin, and the trampling of the sanctuary and the army would last.

questions.q: How long will these things last, this vision about the burnt offering, the sin that brings destruction, the handing over of the sanctuary, and heaven’s army being trampled on?
questions.a: It will last for 2,300 evenings and mornings.

questions.q: What did Daniel do after he saw the vision?
questions.a: He tried to understand it, and then someone who looked like a man appeared in front of him.

questions.q: Who was told to help Daniel understand the vision?
questions.a: Gabriel was told to help Daniel understand the vision.

questions.q: What happened when the angel came near Daniel?
questions.a: Daniel was frightened and fell facedown on the ground. But the angel told him to understand that the vision was about the time of the end.

questions.q: What happened to Daniel while the angel was speaking with him?
questions.a: Daniel fell into a deep sleep with his face to the ground, but the angel touched him and made him stand up again.

questions.q: For when was the vision? What time did it concern?
questions.a: The vision was for the time of wrath. It concerned the fixed time for the end.

questions.q: What did the ram with two horns and the male goat represent in Daniel’s vision?
questions.a: The ram with the two horns represents the kings of Media and Persia. The male goat is the king of Greece.

questions.q: What did the four horns represent, the horns that came in place of the horn that was broken off?
questions.a: The four horns represent four kingdoms that will arise from the nation represented by the horn that was broken off.

questions.q: What kind of king will arise at the end of those kingdoms’ rule?
questions.a: A fierce king will arise who defeats his enemies in battle and who is very deceitful.

questions.q: What will this intelligent, grim-faced king do?
questions.a: He will cause widespread destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy powerful people, people who are holy. He will make deceit prosper under his hand. He will rise up against God, who rules over all earthly kings.

questions.q: What will finally happen to the intelligent, grim-faced king?
questions.a: He will be broken, but not by human power.

questions.q: What did the angel tell Daniel to do with the vision?
questions.a: He told Daniel that the vision was true, but that Daniel should keep it secret because it would not happen for a long time.

questions.q: How did this vision affect Daniel?
questions.a: Daniel was overcome and lay weak for several days, and he was appalled by the vision.

commentary.text: Daniel's vision of the ram and the he-goat. (Dan. 8:1-14) The interpretation of it. (Dan. 8:15-27)

Dan. 8:1-14 God gives Daniel a foresight of the destruction of other kingdoms, which in their day were as powerful as that of Babylon. Could we foresee the changes that shall be when we are gone, we should be less affected with changes in our own day. The ram with two horns was the second empire, that of Media and Persia. He saw this ram overcome by a he-goat. This was Alexander the Great. Alexander, when about thirty-three years of age, and in his full strength, died, and showed the vanity of worldly pomp and power, and that they cannot make a man happy. While men dispute, as in the case of Alexander, respecting the death of some prosperous warrior, it is plain that the great First Cause of all had no more of his plan for him to execute, and therefore cut him off. Instead of that one great horn, there came up four notable ones, Alexander's four chief captains. A little horn became a great persecutor of the church and people of God. It seems that the Mohammedan delusion is here pointed out. It prospered, and at one time nearly destroyed the holy religion God's right hand had planted. It is just with God to deprive those of the privileges of his house who despise and profane them; and to make those know the worth of ordinances by the want of them, who would not know it by the enjoyment of them. Daniel heard the time of this calamity limited and determined; but not the time when it should come. If we would know the mind of God, we must apply to Christ, in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge; not hid from us, but hid for us. There is much difficulty as to the precise time here stated, but the end of it cannot be very distant. God will, for his own glory, see to the cleansing of the church in due time. Christ died to cleanse his church; and he will so cleanse it as to present it blameless to himself.

Dan. 8:15-27 The eternal Son of God stood before the prophet in the appearance of a man, and directed the angel Gabriel to explain the vision. Daniel's fainting and astonishment at the prospect of evils he saw coming on his people and the church, confirm the opinion that long-continued calamities were foretold. The vision being ended, a charge was given to Daniel to keep it private for the present. He kept it to himself, and went on to do the duty of his place. As long as we live in this world we must have something to do in it; and even those whom God has most honoured, must not think themselves above their business. Nor must the pleasure of communion with God take us from the duties of our callings, but we must in them abide with God. All who are intrusted with public business must discharge their trust uprightly; and, amidst all doubts and discouragements, they may, if true believers, look forward to a happy issue. Thus should we endeavour to compose our minds for attending to the duties to which each is appointed, in the church and in the world.
